I looked at your situation and what you would have to read through to attempt to solve this, and it is total shite for a newbie. You don't have the drivers (firmware) needed to make your non-Free/proprietary wifi hardware work, I think.

This will hopefully help:

Download the bottom link here, which is the official legacy support for your hardware:

https://wireless.wiki.kernel.org/_media/en/users/drivers/iwlwifi-4965-ucode-228.61.2.24.tgz

Then, you need to navigate inside that download to the following file:

iwlwifi-4965-2.ucode

That is the firmware you need, but it isn't where you need it, so copy it to your firmware folder using the following commands:

Open a terminal: (Find applications, accessories, terminal) It will give you a text box, then enter:

ls

This will list the files and folders in your current directory. If you can't see the file you just downloaded, then you are in the wrong directory.

When you can see iwlwifi-4965-2.ucode listed, use the following command:

sudo cp iwlwifi-4965-2.ucode /lib/firmware/iwlwifi-4965-2.ucode

sudo means you grant yourself the necessary administrator permissions, cp means copy, and /lib/firmware/ is the folder where firmware is kept.

You might need to reboot afterwards to ensure that the firmware is loaded. You might need a wired connection to reach the internet to download the firmware onto your computer.

I suggest you try and find a local GNU+Linux users group.

There are a few ways forward for you:

1) I think you might already have had that Ubuntu on your computer already, rather than installing it yourself. Try creating a bootable USB drive with a recent version of Ubuntu 18.04

http://releases.ubuntu.com/18.04/ubuntu-18.04-beta2-desktop-amd64.iso

During the installation process, it prompts you, "Do you want additional software, eg for drivers?" This is all non-Free software, but you unfortunately need it, if you want your wi-fi to work, so tick the "Yes" box, and install. Having a working wired connection is needed.

2) Try an alternative distro, for example, Debian GNU/Linux. Debian is more conservative/stable and makes Freedom a greater priority. They have (controversially) made available a "with firmware" DVD, which is convenient for those who need non-Free firmware: I will recommend the KDE desktop one for you, as it is beautiful and in the future I hope you try the KDE-neon distro):

https://cdimage.debian.org/cdimage/unofficial/non-free/cd-including-firmware/9.4.0-live+nonfree/amd64/iso-hybrid/debian-live-9.4.0-amd64-kde+nonfree.iso

That is a live CD, so you should be able to see it in action before installing it. The package you need for your wifi in Debian is iwlegacy:

https://web.archive.org/web/20170913114922/https://wiki.debian.org/iwlegacy

In Debian, the commands are: 

su 
apt install iwlegacy

su means you want super user/administrator privileges. apt is the advanced package tool, which is used to install/remove packages.

Debian is the ultimate in stability for GNU+Linux, and opts for tried and tested packages rather than the latest, bleeding edge versions which might not work so well. It is the father of Ubuntu, and a huge number of other distros, and has legendary security team.

3) The third option... Find a friend who uses GNU+Linux and who will use their experience to help you. It is too much agro for somebody who is just starting.

In future, always go for Free hardware, ideally, you want the ultimate in Free:

https://minifree.org

Which has a Free BIOS using LibreBoot, and a Free fork of Ubuntu: Trisquel GNU/Linux. It uses Linux-Libre, which is a de-blobbed Linux kernel.

https://trisquel.info

Also look at:

https://parabola.nu

Which is a Free fork of the Arch distro, and is far more bleeding edge.

Good luck. Let us know, if you get it working! :)
